## Refined-bar reinforcement (stays READY-TO-FIX; sharpened recommendation)

The refined standard confirms this as the ROOT correction and clarifies the target code. **Do NOT split into several narrow codes.** The one honest principle for branch 6:

- Keep `llm_unavailable` for `isinstance(exc, LLMUnavailableError)` (incl. LLMConfigError) — its scenario set (extra absent, credentials missing/invalid, provider unreachable/rate-limited/refused) accurately fits the name.
- Everything else under `LLMError` → `command_failed`, the existing broad-but-accurate "an unclassified rebar command failure." That code honestly covers the whole residual set (input rejections, tool-loop/budget self-stops, context-window, output defects, and — pending 73d8 — workflow/expression faults) WITHOUT naming a wrong cause.

**Why `command_failed` and not new vocab:** per the 35ab/551b precedent, grow vocabulary only for demonstrated observable need. `command_failed` is not misleading for these scenarios — it makes no false cause claim — so it is an accurate fit, just broad. Finer per-type codes (input_rejected, output_invalid, …) are OPTIONAL and should be filed separately only if a consumer needs the distinction.

Implementation note: narrowing branch 6 to `LLMUnavailableError` is the single change that also fixes 7d47 (load-time WorkflowError) and resolves the 73d8/551b tension (a genuine execute-time outage is an `LLMUnavailableError` and stays `llm_unavailable`; an `ExpressionError` is not, so it correctly falls to `command_failed`).
